He said: "We find eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, each day a thousand years."

Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Shurayk, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, that he said: "The ḥuqb is eighty years, the year is three hundred and sixty days, and the day is a thousand years."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The ḥuqb is eighty years."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, he said: "The ḥuqb is eighty years, the year is three hundred and sixty days, the day is a year or a thousand years" [al-Tabari is doubtful].

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: God said: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, and it is that which has no end; whenever one ḥuqb passes, another ḥuqb comes after it. It was mentioned to us that the ḥuqb is eighty years.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿aḥqāban﴾, he said: "It has reached us that the ḥuqb is eighty years of the years of the Hereafter."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, "No one knows the number of these ages except God, but one ḥuqb is eighty years, the year is three hundred and sixty days, and each day of that is a thousand years."

Others said: One ḥuqb is seventy thousand years.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn ʿAbd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salama narrated to me, from Zuhayr, from Salim, who said: I heard al-Hasan being asked about God's saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, and he said: "As for the ages, there is no count of them except eternity in the Fire; but they mentioned that one ḥuqb is seventy thousand years, each day of those seventy thousand days being like a thousand years of what you count."

ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Amuli narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, he said: "As for the ages, no one knows what they are, but one ḥuqb is seventy thousand years, each day like a thousand years."

It is narrated from Khalid ibn Maʿdan regarding this verse that it refers to the people of the qibla (Muslims).

Mention of those who said that:

ʿAli narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAmir ibn Jashb, from Khalid ibn Maʿdan, regarding His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, and His saying: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾, that both refer to the people of monotheism from among the people of the qibla.

If someone says: What do you say about this report? It is said: What Qatada said from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas about this is more sound. If he says: "Then for the disbelievers there is no punishment except ages," it is said: Indeed al-Rabiʿ and Qatada both said that these ages have no end and no cessation. It may also be that the meaning of it is: remaining therein for ages in this type of punishment, and that they: ﴿will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water and dark, cold liquid﴾. Then when those ages are over, they will have other kinds of punishment beyond that, as God, may His praise be exalted, said in His Book: ﴿And indeed for the transgressors is an evil place of return: Hell, which they will burn in, and wretched is the resting place. This—so let them taste it: scalding water and dark, cold liquid, and other punishments of its kind in pairs﴾. This view is more similar to the meaning of the verse in my opinion.

It has been narrated from Muqatil ibn Hayyan concerning this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salama narrated to us, saying: I asked Abu Muʿadh al-Khurasani about God's saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, and he informed us from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, who said: "It is abrogated (mansukha); it was abrogated by ﴿So We will not increase you except in punishment﴾." There is no meaning to this statement, because His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾ is a report, and reports do not admit abrogation (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation); abrogation occurs only in commands and prohibitions.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink﴾

He says: They will not taste therein any coolness (bard) that cools the heat of the blaze from them, except the dark, cold liquid (ghassaq), nor any drink that quenches them from the intensity of the thirst that is upon them, except scalding water (ḥamīm). Some people of knowledge of the Arabic language have claimed that bard in this place means sleep, and that the meaning of the statement is: They will not taste therein sleep or drink, citing as evidence for this view the saying of al-Kindi:

"Its sips cooled upon me, and the coolness kept me from it, and from its kisses (qublāt), the coolness."

(The report is cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (1:41–42) from this place, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (1:9), attributing it to al-Tabari alone. ʿAwf, who narrated from al-Hasan, is ʿAwf ibn Abi Jamila al-Abdi, known as Ibn al-Aʿrabi, and he is trustworthy and reliable.)

By bard they mean drowsiness (nuʿas), and sleep, if it cools the thirst's burning, then it is said that for this reason it is called bard, though it is not its known name. The interpretation of God's Book is according to the most common usage of the Arabic language, not otherwise.

The exegetes have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water and dark, cold liquid﴾. He made an exception of scalding water from drink and of dark, cold liquid from coolness.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except scalding water and dark, cold liquid﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water that has been heated until its heat reaches its extreme, so it is like molten metal (muhl) that scorches the faces, and no coolness except dark, cold liquid.

The exegetes differed on the meaning of ghassaq. Some of them said: It is what flows from the pus of the people of Hell.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAtiyya ibn Saʿd, regarding His saying: ﴿scalding water and ghassaq﴾, he said: "It is what flows from their skins."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: Abu ʿAmr narrated to us, who said: ʿIkrima claimed that he had told them, regarding His saying: ﴿and ghassaq﴾, he said: "What comes out of their eyes of pus and blood."

Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim and Abu Razin, regarding ﴿scalding water and ghassaq﴾: both said: "The washings of the people of the Fire." That is the wording of Ibn Bashshar; as for Ibn al-Muthanna, he said in his narration: "What flows from their pus."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us again, from ʿAbd al-Rahman, saying the same as Ibn al-Muthanna.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Razin: ﴿and ghassaq﴾, he said: "What flows from their pus."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur and Abu Razin, from Ibrahim, the same.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿ghassaq﴾: "We used to be told that the ghassaq is what flows from between its skin and flesh."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: "It has reached me that it is what flows from their tears."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿and ghassaq﴾, he said: "What flows from their pus from the cold." Sufyan said this, and someone else said: "The tears."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾: "The hamim is the tears of their eyes in the Fire, gathered in the trenches of the Fire, and they are given to drink from it. And the ghassaq is the pus that comes out of their skins, what the Fire melts them with, in basins where it is gathered, and they are given to drink from it."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾, he said: "The ghassaq is what drips from their skins and what flows from their stench."

Others said: The ghassaq is the zamharir (extreme cold).

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾, he says: "The zamharir."

Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa'ib and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾: "That which they cannot bear to taste because of its coldness."

He said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾, he said: "That which they cannot endure because of its cold."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: "The ghassaq is that which cannot be endured because of its cold."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, who said: "The ghassaq is the zamharir."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliya, who said: "The ghassaq is the zamharir."

Others said: It is the stinking, and it is in al-Takhariyya (a region).

Mention of those who said that:

It was reported to me from al-Musayyab ibn Sharik, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Abd Allah ibn Buraida, who said: "The ghassaq, in al-Takhariyya, is the stinking."

In my view, ghassaq is the fa'al pattern, from their saying: "The eye of so-and-so ghasaqat" when its tears flowed, and "the wound ghasaqa" when its pus flowed. From it is God's saying: ﴿and from the evil of the darkening (ghasiq) when it settles﴾, where by ghasiq is meant the night when it covers things and envelops them; what is intended thereby is its onslaught upon things, like the onslaught of a flowing flood. So if ghassaq is what I have described as a flowing thing, then it must be said: What God promised these people, and informed that they would taste in the Hereafter of drink, is the liquid flowing from the zamharir in Hell, which combines with its intense cold a stench.

As:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yaʿmur ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Rushdin ibn Saʿd narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "If a bucket of ghassaq were poured out into this world, it would make the people of this world stink."

I was told from Muhammad ibn Harb, who said: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Abu Qabil, from Abu Malik, from Abd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "Do you know what the ghassaq is?" They said: "God knows best." He said: "It is thick pus. If a drop of it were poured out in the West, it would make the people of the East stink, and if it were poured out in the East, it would make the people of the West stink."

If someone says: You have said that the ghassaq is the zamharir, and the zamharir is extreme cold; so how can the zamharir be flowing? It is said: The cold that cannot be endured or borne takes on the attribute of a flowing thing from the bodies of those people, from pus and purulence.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 78, verses 21–25:

﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾ ﴿for the transgressors, a place of return,﴾ ﴿remaining therein for ages.﴾ ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink,﴾ ﴿except scalding water and dark, cold liquid.﴾

Concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾

By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Indeed, Hell has been a place of watching for its people, those who used to deny in the world both it and the return to God in the Hereafter, and also for others among those who affirm it. The meaning of the statement is: Indeed, Hell has been a place of lying in wait, watching for whoever passes through it and keeping an eye on them.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: Al-Hasan, whenever he recited this verse, ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, would say: "Indeed, at the gate there is a watchman. Whoever comes with a pass will pass through, and whoever does not come with a pass will be detained."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, he said: "No one enters Paradise until he passes through the Fire."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, he said: "It informs us that there is no path to Paradise until one crosses the Fire."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, he said: "On it are three bridges."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿for the transgressors, a place of return﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, Hell is, for those who transgressed in the world, who exceeded the limits of God out of arrogance toward their Lord, a dwelling and a place of return, to which they return, and a destination to which they go, to dwell in it.

The exegetes have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿a place of return﴾, meaning a dwelling and a refuge.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿a place of return﴾, he said: "A place of return and a dwelling."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, these transgressors in the world will remain in Hell, abiding therein for ages.

The readers (qurra') differed in the recitation of His saying: ﴿labithin﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some readers of Kufa, recited it as ﴿labithin﴾ with an alif (lābithīn). The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it as "labithin" without an alif (labithīn). The more eloquent of the two readings, and the one more sound in its grammatical derivation in Arabic, is the reading of the one who recites it with the alif. This is because the Arabs hardly ever use an adjective of the pattern fa'il (ʿafila) and then make it govern something and put it in the accusative by it. They would not say: "This is a man stingy (bakhil) with his wealth," nor "it was difficult (asir) for us," nor "he is a quarrelsome opponent (khasim) to us," because such a pattern as fa'ila does not come as an adjective except to praise or blame, so the praise or blame does not govern anything other than itself. When they want to make such a word govern a noun or something else, they make it an active participle (fā'il) and say: "He is bakhil with his wealth" (bākhil bi-mālihi), and "he is ṭāmi' in what is with us" (ṭāmi' fīmā 'indanā). Therefore I said that lābithīn is more sound in its grammatical derivation in Arabic and more eloquent. I have not deemed lawful the reading of the one who recites labithin, although the other is more eloquent, because the Arabs sometimes make praise govern nouns. A verse of Labid is recited:

"Or a mislah ʿamil, a flank of a smooth-skinned she-ass (samaḥj), with its shoulders having wounds and sores."

So ʿamil governed ʿiḍāda (flank), and if it were an active participle it would have been more eloquent. It is also recited:

"... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... and with the axe, a striker of the heads of the karanif (thistle/hard-headed)."

And from it is the saying of ʿAbbās ibn Mirdas:

"More fearless and more protective of the truth than them, and striking with swords the helmets (qawānis) more than us."

As for al-aḥqāb (ages), it is the plural of ḥuqb, and ḥiqab is the plural of ḥiqba, as the poet said:

"We lived like the two companions of Jadhima for an age (ḥiqba) of time, until it was said: we shall not separate."

So this is plural ḥiqab, and among the uses of aḥqāb whose plural is ḥuqb is God's saying: ﴿or I will continue for a long age (ḥuqb)﴾. So this is the singular of aḥqāb.

The exegetes differed concerning the duration of a ḥuqb. Some of them said: it is a duration of three hundred years.

Others said: rather, the duration of one ḥuqb is eighty years.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: Abu ʿAmr narrated to us, who said: ʿIkrima claimed that he had told them, regarding His saying: ﴿and ghassaq﴾, he said: "What comes out of their eyes of pus and blood."

Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim and Abu Razin, regarding ﴿scalding water and ghassaq﴾: both said: "The washings of the people of the Fire." That is the wording of Ibn Bashshar; as for Ibn al-Muthanna, he said in his narration: "What flows from their pus."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us again, from ʿAbd al-Rahman, saying the same as Ibn al-Muthanna.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Razin: ﴿and ghassaq﴾, he said: "What flows from their pus."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur and Abu Razin, from Ibrahim, the same.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿ghassaq﴾: "We used to be told that the ghassaq is what flows from between its skin and flesh."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: "It has reached me that it is what flows from their tears."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿and ghassaq﴾, he said: "What flows from their pus from the cold." Sufyan said this, and someone else said: "The tears."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾: "The hamim is the tears of their eyes in the Fire, gathered in the trenches of the Fire, and they are given to drink from it. And the ghassaq is the pus that comes out of their skins, what the Fire melts them with, in basins where it is gathered, and they are given to drink from it."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾, he said: "The ghassaq is what drips from their skins and what flows from their stench."

Others said: The ghassaq is the zamharir (extreme cold).

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾, he says: "The zamharir."

Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa'ib and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾: "That which they cannot bear to taste because of its coldness."

He said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿except scalding water and ghassaq﴾, he said: "That which they cannot endure because of its cold."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: "The ghassaq is that which cannot be endured because of its cold."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, who said: "The ghassaq is the zamharir."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliya, who said: "The ghassaq is the zamharir."

Others said: It is the stinking, and it is in al-Takhariyya (a region).

Mention of those who said that:

It was reported to me from al-Musayyab ibn Sharik, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Abd Allah ibn Buraida, who said: "The ghassaq, in al-Takhariyya, is the stinking."

In my view, ghassaq is the fa'al pattern, from their saying: "The eye of so-and-so ghasaqat" when its tears flowed, and "the wound ghasaqa" when its pus flowed. From it is God's saying: ﴿and from the evil of the darkening (ghasiq) when it settles﴾, where by ghasiq is meant the night when it covers things and envelops them; what is intended thereby is its onslaught upon things, like the onslaught of a flowing flood. So if ghassaq is what I have described as a flowing thing, then it must be said: What God promised these people, and informed that they would taste in the Hereafter of drink, is the liquid flowing from the zamharir in Hell, which combines with its intense cold a stench.

As:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yaʿmur ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Rushdin ibn Saʿd narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "If a bucket of ghassaq were poured out into this world, it would make the people of this world stink."

I was told from Muhammad ibn Harb, who said: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Abu Qabil, from Abu Malik, from Abd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "Do you know what the ghassaq is?" They said: "God knows best." He said: "It is thick pus. If a drop of it were poured out in the West, it would make the people of the East stink, and if it were poured out in the East, it would make the people of the West stink."

If someone says: You have said that the ghassaq is the zamharir, and the zamharir is extreme cold; so how can the zamharir be flowing? It is said: The cold that cannot be endured or borne takes on the attribute of a flowing thing from the bodies of those people, from pus and purulence.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 78, verses 21–25:

﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾ ﴿for the transgressors, a place of return,﴾ ﴿remaining therein for ages.﴾ ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink,﴾ ﴿except scalding water and dark, cold liquid.﴾

Concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾

By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Indeed, Hell has been a place of watching for its people, those who used to deny in the world both it and the return to God in the Hereafter, and also for others among those who affirm it. The meaning of the statement is: Indeed, Hell has been a place of lying in wait, watching for whoever passes through it and keeping an eye on them.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: Al-Hasan, whenever he recited this verse, ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, would say: "Indeed, at the gate there is a watchman. Whoever comes with a pass will pass through, and whoever does not come with a pass will be detained."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, he said: "No one enters Paradise until he passes through the Fire."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, he said: "It informs us that there is no path to Paradise until one crosses the Fire."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, he said: "On it are three bridges."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿for the transgressors, a place of return﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, Hell is, for those who transgressed in the world, who exceeded the limits of God out of arrogance toward their Lord, a dwelling and a place of return, to which they return, and a destination to which they go, to dwell in it.

The exegetes have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿a place of return﴾, meaning a dwelling and a refuge.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿a place of return﴾, he said: "A place of return and a dwelling."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, these transgressors in the world will remain in Hell, abiding therein for ages.

The readers (qurra') differed in the recitation of His saying: ﴿labithin﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some readers of Kufa, recited it as ﴿labithin﴾ with an alif (lābithīn). The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it as "labithin" without an alif (labithīn). The more eloquent of the two readings, and the one more sound in its grammatical derivation in Arabic, is the reading of the one who recites it with the alif. This is because the Arabs hardly ever use an adjective of the pattern fa'il (ʿafila) and then make it govern something and put it in the accusative by it. They would not say: "This is a man stingy (bakhil) with his wealth," nor "it was difficult (asir) for us," nor "he is a quarrelsome opponent (khasim) to us," because such a pattern as fa'ila does not come as an adjective except to praise or blame, so the praise or blame does not govern anything other than itself. When they want to make such a word govern a noun or something else, they make it an active participle (fā'il) and say: "He is bakhil with his wealth" (bākhil bi-mālihi), and "he is ṭāmi' in what is with us" (ṭāmi' fīmā 'indanā). Therefore I said that lābithīn is more sound in its grammatical derivation in Arabic and more eloquent. I have not deemed lawful the reading of the one who recites labithin, although the other is more eloquent, because the Arabs sometimes make praise govern nouns. A verse of Labid is recited:

"Or a mislah ʿamil, a flank of a smooth-skinned she-ass (samaḥj), with its shoulders having wounds and sores."

So ʿamil governed ʿiḍāda (flank), and if it were an active participle it would have been more eloquent. It is also recited:

"... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... and with the axe, a striker of the heads of the karanif (thistle/hard-headed)."

And from it is the saying of ʿAbbās ibn Mirdas:

"More fearless and more protective of the truth than them, and striking with swords the helmets (qawānis) more than us."

As for al-aḥqāb (ages), it is the plural of ḥuqb, and ḥiqab is the plural of ḥiqba, as the poet said:

"We lived like the two companions of Jadhima for an age (ḥiqba) of time, until it was said: we shall not separate."

So this is plural ḥiqab, and among the uses of aḥqāb whose plural is ḥuqb is God's saying: ﴿or I will continue for a long age (ḥuqb)﴾. So this is the singular of aḥqāb.

The exegetes differed concerning the duration of a ḥuqb. Some of them said: it is a duration of three hundred years.

Mention of those who said that:

ʿImran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Warith ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from Bashir ibn Ka'b, regarding His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, he said: "It has reached me that a ḥuqb is three hundred years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day a thousand years."

Others said: rather, the duration of one ḥuqb is eighty years.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: ʿAmmar al-Duhni narrated to me, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said to Hilal al-Hajari: "What do you find of the ḥuqb in the revealed Book of God?" He said: "We find eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, each day a thousand years."

Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Shurayk, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, that he said: "The ḥuqb is eighty years, the year is three hundred and sixty days, and the day is a thousand years."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The ḥuqb is eighty years."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, he said: "The ḥuqb is eighty years, the year is three hundred and sixty days, the day is a year or a thousand years" [al-Tabari is doubtful].

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: God said: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, and it is that which has no end; whenever one ḥuqb passes, another ḥuqb comes after it. It was mentioned to us that the ḥuqb is eighty years.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿aḥqāban﴾, he said: "It has reached us that the ḥuqb is eighty years of the years of the Hereafter."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, "No one knows the number of these ages except God, but one ḥuqb is eighty years, the year is three hundred and sixty days, and each day of that is a thousand years."

Others said: One ḥuqb is seventy thousand years.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn ʿAbd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salama narrated to me, from Zuhayr, from Salim, who said: I heard al-Hasan being asked about God's saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, and he said: "As for the ages, there is no count of them except eternity in the Fire; but they mentioned that one ḥuqb is seventy thousand years, each day of those seventy thousand days being like a thousand years of what you count."

ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Amuli narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, he said: "As for the ages, no one knows what they are, but one ḥuqb is seventy thousand years, each day like a thousand years."

It is narrated from Khalid ibn Maʿdan regarding this verse that it refers to the people of the qibla (Muslims).

Mention of those who said that:

ʿAli narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAmir ibn Jashb, from Khalid ibn Maʿdan, regarding His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, and His saying: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾, that both refer to the people of monotheism from among the people of the qibla.

If someone says: What do you say about this report? It is said: What Qatada said from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas about this is more sound. If he says: "Then for the disbelievers there is no punishment except ages," it is said: Indeed al-Rabiʿ and Qatada both said that these ages have no end and no cessation. It may also be that the meaning of it is: remaining therein for ages in this type of punishment, and that they: ﴿will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water and dark, cold liquid﴾. Then when those ages are over, they will have other kinds of punishment beyond that, as God, may His praise be exalted, said in His Book: ﴿And indeed for the transgressors is an evil place of return: Hell, which they will burn in, and wretched is the resting place. This—so let them taste it: scalding water and dark, cold liquid, and other punishments of its kind in pairs﴾. This view is more similar to the meaning of the verse in my opinion.

It has been narrated from Muqatil ibn Hayyan concerning this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salama narrated to us, saying: I asked Abu Muʿadh al-Khurasani about God's saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, and he informed us from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, who said: "It is abrogated (mansukha); it was abrogated by ﴿So We will not increase you except in punishment﴾." There is no meaning to this statement, because His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾ is a report, and reports do not admit abrogation (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation); abrogation occurs only in commands and prohibitions.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink﴾

He says: They will not taste therein any coolness (bard) that cools the heat of the blaze from them, except the dark, cold liquid (ghassaq), nor any drink that quenches them from the intensity of the thirst that is upon them, except scalding water (ḥamīm). Some people of knowledge of the Arabic language have claimed that bard in this place means sleep, and that the meaning of the statement is: They will not taste therein sleep or drink, citing as evidence for this view the saying of al-Kindi:

"Its sips cooled upon me, and the coolness kept me from it, and from its kisses (qublāt), the coolness."

(The report is cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (1:41–42) from this place, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (1:9), attributing it to al-Tabari alone. ʿAwf, who narrated from al-Hasan, is ʿAwf ibn Abi Jamila al-Abdi, known as Ibn al-Aʿrabi, and he is trustworthy and reliable.)

By bard they mean drowsiness (nuʿas), and sleep, if it cools the thirst's burning, then it is said that for this reason it is called bard, though it is not its known name. The interpretation of God's Book is according to the most common usage of the Arabic language, not otherwise.

The exegetes have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water and dark, cold liquid﴾. He made an exception of scalding water from drink and of dark, cold liquid from coolness.

* *

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water that has been heated until its heat reaches its extreme, so it is like molten metal (muhl) that scorches the faces, and no coolness except dark, cold liquid.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 26–30:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿A fitting recompense (jaza'an wifaqa).﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: This punishment with which these disbelievers are punished in the Hereafter is a recompense their Lord has done to them, meaning: a reward for them for their evil deeds and words which they used to do in the world. It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "This punishment agreed (wafaqa) with this knowledge in agreement (wifaqan)."

Interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿A fitting recompense﴾, he said: it agrees with their deeds.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 26–30:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿A fitting recompense (jaza'an wifaqa).﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: This punishment with which these disbelievers are punished in the Hereafter is a recompense their Lord has done to them, meaning: a reward for them for their evil deeds and words which they used to do in the world. Interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, they did not expect a reckoning﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, these disbelievers in the world did not fear being called to account by God in the Hereafter for His blessings upon them, His kindness to them, and their poor gratitude to Him for that.

Interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Then some of them said to others: What is wrong with him? ﴿Has he invented a lie against God, or is there madness in him?﴾ The man is mad when he tells us this.

* *

And His words: ﴿And they denied Our signs, a denial (kiddaban)﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: These disbelievers denied Our proofs and evidences with denial. It is said: ﴿kiddaban﴾, and He did not say "takdhiban," as a leading to its verb.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: it was said this way because its verb (fa'ala) is of four letters, so he wanted to make it like the pattern af'ala, whose verbal noun is if'al, so he said kiddaban, making it match the number of letters of its verbal noun. He said: On this analogy you say qatala qitalan. He said: and this is from the speech of the Arabs. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: this is an eloquent Yemeni dialect; they say kadhdhabtu bihi kiddaban, and kharraqtu al-qamis khirraqan, and every fa'ala's verbal noun in their dialect is fi'al with doubling. He said: A Bedouin once said to me on al-Marwa, asking my opinion: "Is shaving more beloved to you or trimming?" He said: And one of the Banu Kilab recited to me:

It has long kept me from my companions,
and from needs whose fulfilment is from my healing.

Readers have agreed on doubling the dhal in al-kidhdhab (the liar) in this place. Al-Kisa'i alone used to lighten the second letter, in His words: ﴿They hear therein no idle talk nor lying (kidhdhaban)﴾, and he said: it is from their saying "kadhabtuhu kidhdhaban and mukadhaba," and he doubled this one, and he said that His words "kadhdhabu" (they denied) restrict "al-kidhdhab" to the verbal noun.

That is: and vineyards of grapevines. By mentioning the grapevines he dispensed with mentioning the vineyards.

He says: and maidens with rising breasts of one age.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing (dihaq)﴾

He says: and a cup full and following one another in abundance and fullness for those who drink from it. Its origin is from al-dahq, which is the continuous pressing upon a person with force and violence; likewise the cup dihaq is one that follows its drinkers in abundance and fullness.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Ibn Hibban mentioned him in Kitab al-Thiqat (p. 54) in the class of the Companions, and said: "It is said that he had companionship." al-Hafiz transmitted this in al-Lisan from Ibn Hibban, but erred in claiming that he mentioned him "among the reliable Successors."

He says: Indeed, for the God-fearing is a deliverance (manja) from the Fire to Paradise, and an escape from it to them toward it, and success in what they sought.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing is a place of success﴾: He said: They succeeded by being saved from the Fire.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing is a place of success﴾: "Yes, by God, a place of success from the Fire to Paradise, and from the punishment of God to His mercy."

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing is a place of success﴾: He said: A place of success from the Fire to Paradise.

Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing is a place of success﴾: He says: a place of recreation [[Hadith 151 — the chain of this report has already been shown to be weak at 137. Muhammad ibn al-Ala, the shaykh of al-Tabari, is Abu Kurayb himself in the previous chain, sometimes named and sometimes given his kunya. This report was transmitted by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 1: 43, by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 11, and by al-Shawkani in his tafsir called Fath al-Qadir 1: 10, and they also attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim in his tafsir.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿gardens﴾

The gardens (hada'iq) are an explanation and elaboration of the place of success (mafaz). It is permissible for it to be an explanation of it, because mafaz is a verbal noun from the speaker's saying: "So-and-so succeeded in this thing," when he sought it and attained it. So it is as if it were said: Indeed, for the God-fearing is attainment of what they sought: gardens and grapevines. The hada'iq is the plural of hadiqah, which means orchards of palm trees and grapevines and trees enclosed by walls surrounding them; a garden is called a hadiqah because the walls encircle it (ihdaq). If the walls do not surround it, it is not called a hadiqah. Its encirclement by them is its enfolding of it.

* *

His saying: ﴿and grapevines﴾

That is: and vineyards of grapevines. By mentioning the grapevines he dispensed with mentioning the vineyards.

* *

His saying: ﴿and full-breasted maidens of equal age﴾

He says: and maidens with rising breasts of one age.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and full-breasted maidens﴾: He says: maidens with rising breasts.

* *

His saying: ﴿of equal age﴾

He says: of equal state.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and full-breasted maidens of equal age﴾: He means: women of equal state.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and full-breasted maidens of equal age﴾: He said: maidens with rising breasts, of equal age, meaning they are of one age.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, then he described what is in Paradise: ﴿gardens and grapevines﴾ ﴿and full-breasted maidens of equal age﴾, meaning by that women of equal age, of one age.

Abbas ibn Muhammad told me, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The kawa'ib are the nawahid (those with rising breasts).

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and full-breasted maidens of equal age﴾: He said: The kawa'ib are those whose breasts have risen and whose nipples have become prominent; and he said: atrab means equal, as one says: "So-and-so is the peer (tirb) of so-and-so." He said: The atrab are the peers (liddat).

Nasr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and full-breasted maidens of equal age﴾: peers (liddat).

* *

His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing (dihaq)﴾

He says: and a cup full and following one another in abundance and fullness for those who drink from it. Its origin is from al-dahq, which is the continuous pressing upon a person with force and violence; likewise the cup dihaq is one that follows its drinkers in abundance and fullness.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi told me, saying: Musa ibn Umayr related to us, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿a cup overflowing﴾: He said: full.

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas being asked about ﴿a cup overflowing﴾; he said: "Successive." Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: "That which follows one another."

Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: He says: full.

Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, saying: Humayd al-Tawil related to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, regarding His saying: ﴿a cup overflowing﴾: He said: "Continuous" (damadim) [[Hadith 152 — Ibn Kathir transmitted it 1: 43 with this chain of al-Tabari, and al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 11, attributing it to al-Tabari, al-Hakim in Tarikh Nishapur, and al-Daylami "with a weak chain". As for Baqiyya ibn al-Walid, the truth is that he is trustworthy; they only criticized him for tadlis, and that has no place here, since he explicitly stated hearing.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: He said: full.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, similarly.

Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: He said: the full and successive.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: He said: successive.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will hear therein no idle talk or lying﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: They will not hear in Paradise idle talk, meaning vain speech, nor lying (kidhdhab), meaning no mutual falsehood, that is, none of them will lie to another. The reciters in the cities read kidhdhab with a doubled dhal, as I explained in His saying: ﴿and they denied Our signs with complete denial (kidhdhaban)﴾, except al-Kisa'i, who read it lightly (kidhab) for the reason I described before. Doubling is more beloved to me than lightening, and the recitation is with doubling, and I do not regard reciting it with lightening as valid, because the consensus of the reciting authorities is against it. As evidence for the lightened form is the verse of al-A'sha:

"I affirmed her and I denied her, and a man benefits from his lying."

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said regarding His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: dihaq: successive.

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: He said: the successive.

Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: He said: the full and successive.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: He said: successive.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will hear therein no idle talk or lying﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: They will not hear in Paradise idle talk, meaning vain speech, nor lying (kidhdhab), meaning no mutual falsehood, that is, none of them will lie to another. The reciters in the cities read kidhdhab with a doubled dhal, as I explained in His saying: ﴿and they denied Our signs with complete denial (kidhdhaban)﴾, except al-Kisa'i, who read it lightly (kidhab) for the reason I described before. Doubling is more beloved to me than lightening, and the recitation is with doubling, and I do not regard reciting it with lightening as valid, because the consensus of the reciting authorities is against it. As evidence for the lightened form is the verse of al-A'sha:

"I affirmed her and I denied her, and a man benefits from his lying."

[[Report 153 — This chain is sound, but whether it is sound or weak it has no value, since it ends at Ka'b al-Ahbar. Ka'b's statements were never proof, in tafsir or otherwise. "al-Sadafi," with a fatha on the sad and a kasra on the dal (unmarked), is a nisba to "al-Sadaf," a tribe of Himyar that settled in Egypt. "al-Sulayli" is Abd Allah ibn Damra al-Sulayli, a reliable Successor.

And the interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿idle talk and lying﴾: He said: vanity and sin.

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿They will hear therein no idle talk or lying﴾: He said: It is thus, there is in it neither idle talk nor lying.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 36–38:

ال​قول في تأويل قوله تعالى: ﴿جَزَاءً مِنْ رَبِّكَ عَطَاءً حِسَابًا (٣٦) رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الرَّحْمَنِ لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَابًا (٣٧) يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ وَقَالَ صَوَابًا (٣٨)﴾.

On the discourse concerning the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of meaning) of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿A reward from your Lord, a gift, a reckoning (36). Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful; they cannot address Him (37). On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, none will speak except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will speak rightly (38).﴾

His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿a reward from your Lord﴾ mean: God gives those pious ones what He has described in these verses as a reward from your Lord for their deeds, in return for their obedience to Him in this world.

* *

As for His words ﴿a gift﴾:

It means: a bounty from God to them with that reward, since He rewarded them tenfold for one good deed in some cases, and seven hundredfold for one in others. This increase, although it is a reward, is also a gift from God.

* *

As for His words ﴿a reckoning﴾:

It means: an accounting of them for their deeds done for God in this world.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, here meaning the scholars of Qur'anic exegesis) have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿a reward from your Lord, a gift, a reckoning﴾: He said: "A gift from Him, a reckoning for what they did."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿a reward from your Lord, a gift, a reckoning﴾: that is, a abundant gift; He rewarded them for little deeds with great, everlasting good.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿a gift, a reckoning﴾: He said: "An abundant gift." And Mujahid said: "A gift from God, a reckoning for their deeds."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say concerning God's words ﴿a reward from your Lord, a gift, a reckoning﴾, then he recited: ﴿Indeed, for the pious is a place of success: gardens and grapevines, and maidens of equal age...﴾ up to ﴿a gift, a reckoning﴾. He said: "This is a reward for their deeds; the gift that He gave them, they did for it only one, and He rewarded them ten. And he recited the words of God: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾, and he recited the words of God: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains, and God multiplies for whom He wills﴾." He said: "He increases for whom He wills. All of this is a gift; it was not deeds that He reckoned for them. He rewarded them for it as if they had done it for Him. They did not do it; they did only ten, and He gave them a hundred, and they did a hundred, and He gave them a thousand. All of this is a gift, and the first deed was [their own]; then He reckoned that as if they had done it, and rewarded them as He rewarded them for what they did."

* *

As for His words ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful﴾:

His, the Exalted's, words mean: the reward from your Lord, the Lord of the seven heavens, the earth, and what is between them of creation.

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read ﴿Rabbu al-samawati wa al-ard wa ma baynahuma al-Rahmanu﴾, with the nominative case in both. Some people of Basra and some Kufans read ﴿Rabbi﴾ in the genitive and ﴿al-Rahmanu﴾ in the nominative. Both readings have a correct meaning in our view, and whichever reading the reciter uses is correct. However, the genitive for "Rabb" is more preferable to me, because it is closer to His words ﴿a reward from your Lord﴾. As for ﴿al-Rahman﴾ in the nominative, it is better because it is further removed from that.

* *

As for His words ﴿the Most Merciful; they cannot address Him﴾:

His, the Exalted's, words mean: none of His creatures will be able to address the Most Merciful on the Day of Resurrection, except whoever He permits among them, and that one will speak rightly.

The people of ta'wil have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿they cannot address Him﴾: He said: "Speech."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿they cannot address Him﴾: that is, speech.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿they cannot address Him﴾: "They cannot address God. The one who addresses (mukhatib) is the one who disputes, the opponent who argues with his companion."

* *

As for His words ﴿On the Day when the Spirit stands﴾:

The people of knowledge differed over the meaning of "the Spirit" (al-ruh) in this place. Some of them said: it is an angel, one of the greatest of the angels in creation.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani related to me, saying: Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Spirit is an angel in the fourth heaven, greater than the heavens, the mountains, and the angels. He glorifies God twelve thousand glorifications every day, and God creates from each glorification an angel of the angels, who will come on the Day of Resurrection in a row by himself."

'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand﴾: He said: "He is an angel, the greatest of the angels in creation."

Others said: it is Gabriel, peace be upon him.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, ﴿On the Day when the Spirit stands﴾: He said: "Gabriel, peace be upon him."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Dahhak, ﴿On the Day when the Spirit stands﴾: He said: "The Spirit: Gabriel, peace be upon him."

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Sha'bi, ﴿On the Day when the Spirit stands﴾: He said: "The Spirit is Gabriel, peace be upon him."

Others said: it is a creation from among God's creation in the form of the children of Adam.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The Spirit is a creation in the form of the children of Adam; they eat and drink."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muslim, from Mujahid, who said: "The Spirit: a creation who have hands and feet, and I think he said: and heads, who eat food; they are not angels."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, who said: "They resemble people, and they are not people."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Mujahid, who said: "The Spirit is a creation like the creation of Adam."

Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to me, saying: my father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, concerning His words ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks﴾: He said: "The Spirit is a creation from among God's creation who are multiplied many times over the angels; they have hands and feet."

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, client of Umm Hani', ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand﴾: He said: "The Spirit: a creation like people, and they are not people."

Others said: they are the children of Adam.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿On the Day when the Spirit stands﴾: He said: "They are the children of Adam," and this is the view of al-Hasan.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿On the Day when the Spirit stands﴾: He said: "The Spirit: the children of Adam." Qatadah said: "This is something Ibn 'Abbas used to conceal."

Others said: it was said that it refers to the spirits of the children of Adam.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, none will speak﴾: He said: "It means when the spirits of people stand with the angels between the two blasts, before the spirits are returned to the bodies."

Others said: it is the Qur'an.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "My father used to say: the Spirit is the Qur'an." And he recited: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾.

The correct statement is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that His creatures will not have power to address Him on the Day when the Spirit stands, and the Spirit is a creation from among His creation. It is possible that it is some of these things that have been mentioned, and God knows best which of them it is. No report has come establishing that any one of them is meant to the exclusion of others, which must be accepted, nor is there any proof indicating it. Ignorance of it does no harm.

It was also said: it is two rows (simatan).

Mention of those who said that:

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Mansur ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His words ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, none will speak except whom the Most Merciful permits﴾: He said: "They are two rows [[Hadith 154 – its isnad is sound. 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Abdawayh Abu al-Hasan al-Kharraz, a teacher of al-Tabari: trustworthy, biographed in Tarikh Baghdad 11: 374–375. The name "al-Kharraz" is written in al-Tabari's text with a kha and a ra and a final zay; in Tarikh Baghdad it is "al-Khazzaz" with two zays, and we were unable to decide between them. Muslim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jarmi is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan 6: 32 under the name "Muslim ibn Abi Muslim" without his father's name, and he is the same person. Al-Khatib ascribed him in Tarikh Baghdad 13: 100, saying: "Muslim ibn Abi Muslim al-Jarmi, who is Muslim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman," and said: "He was trustworthy, settled in Tarsus, and died there." "Al-Jarmi" is written in the manuscripts of al-Tabari and Lisan al-Mizan as "al-Harmi" without dots, but they did not specify its vowelling. Their custom in such cases is to specify the rare and unusual vowelling and to leave the common vowelling that follows the usual form. The usual form of this writing is "al-Jarmi" with a jim, and that is how it is written in Tarikh Baghdad; we have preferred it on the basis of this or that. Muhammad ibn Mus'ab al-Qarqasani and Mubarak ibn Fadalah are disputed; we have preferred the authentication of both in the commentary on the Musnad: the first at 3048, the second at 521. Al-Hasan is al-Basri, and we have established in the commentary on Sahih Ibn Hibban, at hadith 132, that he heard from al-Aswad ibn Sari'.

al-Suyuti mentioned this hadith in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 12, from the tafsir of al-Tabari. Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad, in a shortened form with similar meaning, at 15650 (3: 435, Halabi), from Rawh ibn 'Ubadah, from 'Awf ibn Abi Jamilah, from al-Hasan, from al-Aswad ibn Sari', who said: "I said: O Messenger of God, shall I not recite to you praises with which I have praised my Lord? He said: 'Indeed your Lord loves praise.'" This is a sound isnad; all its narrators are trustworthy and reliable. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 1: 43, from the Musnad. Al-Suyuti likewise mentioned it, ascribing it also to al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim, and others.

Ahmad also narrated it at 15654, and al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad: 51, in a similar form, in a lengthy account, from the narration of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah from al-Aswad ibn Sari'.

Its meaning is established and sound, from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud in the Musnad, 4153: "None is more jealous than God, and therefore He has forbidden indecencies, whether apparent or hidden. And none loves praise more than God, and therefore He has praised Himself." It was also narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others.]] to the Lord of the worlds on the Day of Resurrection: a row of the Spirit, and a row of the angels.

* *

As for His words ﴿they will not speak except whom the Most Merciful permits﴾:

It was said: they will be permitted to speak when the people of the Fire are ordered to the Fire and the people of the Garden to the Garden.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, saying: Abu 'Amr narrated to us, who tells stories among Tayy, from 'Ikrimah, and he recited this verse: ﴿except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he speaks rightly﴾, and said: "People of the Fire will pass by angels, and [the angels] will say: 'Where are you taking these?' It will be said: 'To the Fire.' They will say: 'For what their hands have earned; God did not wrong them.' People of the Garden will pass by angels, and it will be said: 'Where are you taking these?' They will say: 'To the Garden.' They will say: 'By the mercy of God you have entered the Garden.' He said: 'Then they will be permitted to speak,' or something like that."

Others said: ﴿except whom the Most Merciful permits﴾ with monotheism (tawhid), ﴿and he speaks rightly﴾ in this world, by affirming God's oneness.

Mention of those who said that:

'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he speaks rightly﴾: He said: "That is, except whom the Lord permits, by the testimony that there is no god but God, and it is the utmost of what is right."

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and he speaks rightly﴾: He said: "Truth in this world, and acting upon it."

'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Salih, concerning His words ﴿except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he speaks rightly﴾: He said: "There is no god but God."

Abu Hafs said: "I related this to Yahya ibn Sa'id, and he said: 'I wrote it down from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Abu Mu'awiyah.'"

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, concerning His words ﴿except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he speaks rightly﴾: He said: "There is no god but God."

The correct statement on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed about His creatures that they will not speak on the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, except whom the Most Merciful permits among them to speak, and he speaks rightly. It is obligatory to say it as He informed, since He did not inform us in His Book, nor through the tongue of His Messenger, that He meant by that one particular kind of rightness. The apparent meaning admits all of it.

It will be said: 'To the Fire.' They will say: 'For what their hands have earned; God did not wrong them.' People of the Garden will pass by angels, and it will be said: 'Where are you taking these?' They will say: 'To the Garden.' They will say: 'By the mercy of God you have entered the Garden.' He said: 'Then they will be permitted to speak,' or something like that."

Others said: ﴿except whom the Most Merciful permits﴾ with monotheism (tawhid), ﴿and he speaks rightly﴾ in this world, by affirming God's oneness.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Hafs said: "I related this to Yahya ibn Sa'id, and he said: 'I wrote it down from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Abu Mu'awiyah.'"

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, concerning His words ﴿except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he speaks rightly﴾: He said: "There is no god but God."

The correct statement on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed about His creatures that they will not speak on the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, except whom the Most Merciful permits among them to speak, and he speaks rightly. It is obligatory to say it as He informed, since He did not inform us in His Book, nor through the tongue of His Messenger, that He meant by that one particular kind of rightness. The apparent meaning admits all of it.

ال​قول في تأويل قوله تعالى: ﴿جَزَاءً مِنْ رَبِّكَ عَطَاءً حِسَابًا (٣٦) رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الرَّحْمَنِ لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَابًا (٣٧) يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ وَقَالَ صَوَابًا (٣٨)﴾.

On the discourse concerning the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of meaning) of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿A reward from your Lord, a gift, a reckoning (36). Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful; they cannot address Him (37). On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, none will speak except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will speak rightly (38).﴾

His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿a reward from your Lord﴾ mean: God gives those pious ones what He has described in these verses as a reward from your Lord for their deeds, in return for their obedience to Him in this world.

* *

As for His words ﴿a gift﴾:

It means: a bounty from God to them with that reward, since He rewarded them tenfold for one good deed in some cases, and seven hundredfold for one in others. This increase, although it is a reward, is also a gift from God.

* *

As for His words ﴿a reckoning﴾:

It means: an accounting of them for their deeds done for God in this world.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, here meaning the scholars of Qur'anic exegesis) have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿a reward from your Lord, a gift, a reckoning﴾: He said: "A gift from Him, a reckoning for what they did."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿a reward from your Lord, a gift, a reckoning﴾: that is, a abundant gift; He rewarded them for little deeds with great, everlasting good.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿a gift, a reckoning﴾: He said: "An abundant gift." And Mujahid said: "A gift from God, a reckoning for their deeds."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say concerning God's words ﴿a reward from your Lord, a gift, a reckoning﴾, then he recited: ﴿Indeed, for the pious is a place of success: gardens and grapevines, and maidens of equal age...﴾ up to ﴿a gift, a reckoning﴾. He said: "This is a reward for their deeds; the gift that He gave them, they did for it only one, and He rewarded them ten. And he recited the words of God: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾, and he recited the words of God: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains, and God multiplies for whom He wills﴾." He said: "He increases for whom He wills. All of this is a gift; it was not deeds that He reckoned for them. He rewarded them for it as if they had done it for Him. They did not do it; they did only ten, and He gave them a hundred, and they did a hundred, and He gave them a thousand. All of this is a gift, and the first deed was [their own]; then He reckoned that as if they had done it, and rewarded them as He rewarded them for what they did."

* *

As for His words ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful﴾:

His, the Exalted's, words mean: the reward from your Lord, the Lord of the seven heavens, the earth, and what is between them of creation.

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read ﴿Rabbu al-samawati wa al-ard wa ma baynahuma al-Rahmanu﴾, with the nominative case in both. Some people of Basra and some Kufans read ﴿Rabbi﴾ in the genitive and ﴿al-Rahmanu﴾ in the nominative. Both readings have a correct meaning in our view, and whichever reading the reciter uses is correct. However, the genitive for "Rabb" is more preferable to me, because it is closer to His words ﴿a reward from your Lord﴾. As for ﴿al-Rahman﴾ in the nominative, it is better because it is further removed from that.

* *

As for His words ﴿the Most Merciful; they cannot address Him﴾:

His, the Exalted's, words mean: none of His creatures will be able to address the Most Merciful on the Day of Resurrection, except whoever He permits among them, and that one will speak rightly.

The people of ta'wil have said what is similar to what we have said.
