Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and he speaks rightly﴾: He said: "Truth in this world, and acting upon it."

'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Salih, concerning His words ﴿except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he speaks rightly﴾: He said: "There is no god but God."

Abu Hafs said: "I related this to Yahya ibn Sa'id, and he said: 'I wrote it down from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Abu Mu'awiyah.'"

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, concerning His words ﴿except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he speaks rightly﴾: He said: "There is no god but God."

The correct statement on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed about His creatures that they will not speak on the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, except whom the Most Merciful permits among them to speak, and he speaks rightly. It is obligatory to say it as He informed, since He did not inform us in His Book, nor through the tongue of His Messenger, that He meant by that one particular kind of rightness. The apparent meaning admits all of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 39–40:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿That is the true Day. So whoever wills may take to his Lord a return.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: ﴿That [is] the Day﴾ meaning the Day of Resurrection, the Day on which the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows. ﴿The true [Day]﴾ means: it is a truth that will certainly occur, with no doubt about it.

And His words: ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a return﴾

That is: whoever of His servants wills, let him take, by affirming this true Day, preparing for it, and acting by what brings salvation from its terrors, a return to his Lord. ﴿A return﴾ means a place of return (marji'). It is a maf'al form from their saying: "So-and-so returned (āba) from his journey," as ʿUbayd said:

"Every absent one returns, but the absent one of death does not return."

[[See what we wrote earlier: 126, on the meaning of "lā tamāni'" (they do not prevent).]]

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a return﴾, he said: They take to Allah a return by obeying Him and by what brings them near to Him.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿to his Lord a return﴾, he said: a way.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿a return﴾, he said: a place of return, a dwelling.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾

That is: We have warned you, O people, of a punishment that has drawn near to you and is close. It is ﴿the Day when a man will look﴾, the believer, ﴿at what his hands have sent forth﴾ of good he earned in the world, or of evil he committed beforehand, so he hopes for Allah's reward for his righteous deeds and fears His punishment for his evil ones.

The people of ta'wil said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿the Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth﴾, he said: the man is the believer, who guards against the minor sin and fears the major sin.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Jahhadah, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿the Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth﴾, he said: the man is the believer.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Jahhadah, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿the Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth﴾, he said: the man is the believer.

And His words: ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: and the disbeliever will say on that Day, wishing for what he meets of the punishment of Allah which He has prepared for His disbelieving companions: "Would that I were dust," like the beasts which were made into dust.

The people of ta'wil said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy narrated to us, both saying: Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Mughirah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the hide will be stretched out, and the beasts, cattle and wild animals will be gathered. Then retribution will take place among the beasts; the hornless sheep will be avenged against the horned sheep that gored it. When He finishes the retribution among the beasts, He will say to them: 'Be dust.' At that moment the disbeliever will say: 'Would that I were dust!'"

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, who said: and Jaʿfar ibn Burqan narrated to me, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Indeed Allah will gather all creatures, every beast, bird and human. He will say to the animals and birds: 'Be dust.' At that moment the disbeliever will say: 'Would that I were dust!'"

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah judges between His creatures, jinn, humans and beasts. On that Day He will exact retribution for the hornless from the horned, until no claim remains of one against another. Then Allah says: 'Be dust!' At that moment the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust!'"

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿the Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾ He said: he is the one who is destroyed, the squanderer, the helpless. What prevents him from saying this, when the defects of his deeds have been exposed to him and he has met the Merciful while He is angry with him? So on that Day he wishes for death, and there was nothing in the world more hateful to him than death.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Abu al-Zinad ʿAbd Allah ibn Dhakwan, who said: When judgment is passed among people and the people of the Fire are ordered to the Fire, it will be said to the believing jinn and the other nations apart from the children of Adam: "Return to dust!" When the disbelievers see them having returned to dust, the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust, would that I were dust!"

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding His words: ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾ He said: when it is said to the beasts, "Be dust!", the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!"

End of the commentary on Surah ʿAmma Yatasa'alun.
